Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business

  1
 session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

adjournment.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

  8
 PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

PURPOSE:  To educate  the Cornrnunity  and Council  on the current  state of the City's  budget
and the structural  deficit  that currently  exists.  A description  of potential  budget  cuts to services
will  be presented  and an outline  of how a Utility  Users Tax measure  is constructed  with  a sample
version  will  be presented.  Resolutions  have been prepared  for discussion  and possible  adoption  for

2026 to adopt an Ordinance  for a Utility  Users Tax measure,  subject  to voter  approval.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopting  a Resolution  declaring  a Fiscal  Emergency;
  b,  Adopting  a Resolution  calling  a Special  Election,  request  that the Los Angeles  County
  Board  of  Supervisors  ("Board  of  Supervisors")  authorize  the  Los  Angeles  County
  Registrar-Recorder  / County  Clerk  ("County  Elections  Official")  to render  all services
  necessary  to conduct  the Election,  allow  for Ballot  Arguments,  and an Impartial  Analysis;
  and
  c.  Reviewing  the draft  Ordinance  for voter  consideration  of the Utility  Users Tax.

FISCALIMPACT:  E1ectionexpensesareexpectedtobeapproximately$258,457andwerenot
included  in the current  fiscal  budget.  Election  costs will  be funded  from  available  General  Fund
reserves.

NOTICING  REQUIREMENTS:  None required.

ANALYSIS:  The City  has been able to sustain  a high  level  of community  services  and retain
quality  City staff and services  providers  by actively  pursuing  and recovering  "one-time"  revenues
to fill  the City's  gowing  structural  deficit.  During  this time,  revenues  within  the City's  General
Fund,  sales tax,  property  tax,  and Vehicle  License  Fees remained  static  with  some  growth  in
property  tax, but with  limited  or no growth  in the other  General  Fund  revenue  sources.  More

  I

  10
 recently, all Cities are facing a significant downward adjustment to revenue from the current tariff
challenges and the downward trend in the economy. South Gate, like most other cities, is being
significantly impacted by these trends. The rising costs for energy, materials, supplies and services
along with limited growth in revenue have contributed to the City's structural deficit, which is now
projected to reach $9,000,000 for the coming fiscal year.

Reeap of Adopted Budget
As reported to the City Council on July 22, 2025, the General Fund unassigned balance was
projected to be $3,135,356 at July 1, 2025. General Fund revenues are budgeted at $70,943,552,
an amount insufficient to sustain current service levels without reliance on one-time measures.
Expenditures are budgeted at $78,157,559 for fiscal year 2025-26, resulting in a structural shortfall
of over $7 million.

Due to the exhaustion of prior one-time federal relief funds; legally constrained growth in core
revenues under Proposition 13,, softening and volatile sales tax receipts; declining interest earnings
resulting from reduced fund balances; and substantial, non-discretionary increases in pension
contributions, insurance premiums, and inflation-driven  operating costs, the City's  ongoing
expenditures  materially  exceed its recurring  revenues.

As a result, tlie City is experiencing a structural operating deficit exceeding $7 million in FY 2025-
26, which is being temporarily mitigated through the use of reserves and interfund transfers. These
measures are non-recurring and unsustainable. Based on the City's adopted multi-year financial
forecast, the General Fund deficit is projected to increase to more than $9 million in FY 2026-27,
atwhichpoint remaining discretionaryreserves will be insufficient to support continued operations
at current  service  levels.

Absent immediate action, the continued depletion of limited General Fund reserves will impair the
City's ability to maintain essential public safety, infrastructure, and community services, thereby
posing a current and immediate threat to the public health, safety, and welfare. Delay in addressing
this condition would result in severe budget cuts that will create significant cuts to current services
currently offered by the City. If no additional revenue is found by the end of the current 25/26
Fiscal Year, a $9,000,000 cut to City services will be required. This cut will impact all general
fund services including services provided by the Police, Parks and Recreation, Community
Development, and Public Works departments.

City's  Actions  to Close  the Budget  Deficit
The City Council and City staff have not stood idly by knowing  that a fiscal crisis was coming.  To
be fiscally  responsible,  the City  has done the following:
  *  Reorganized  and consolidated  Departments  to create more efficiency.
  *  Increased fees for general services, and increased  sewer rates to eliminate  the general  fund
  from  subsidizing  that service.
  *  Enacted  a personnel  hiring  freeze for non-essential  functions  and services.
  *  Reviewed staff salary allocations to maximize  the use of water and special  funding  sources.
  *  Reviewed  City  operations  for operational  and cost efficiencies.

  2

  11
 City staff and City  Council  continue  to review  operations  and reduce City costs; unfortunately,  the
scope  and size of the General  Fund deficit  cannot be solved  with cost-cutting  measures  alone.

Potential  Revenue  Enhancement  Measure  to Protect  and Maintain  Vital  Services
The General  Fund  deficit  is approximately  9.2%  of the overall  General  Fund budget,  even with
the reductions  noted  above.  To address  the $7.21  million  structural  deficit  will  require  a new
revenue  source.  Without  a strong  and reliable  revenue  source, the City will  not be able to maintain
and improve  City  services  such as police  anti-gang  and anti-drug  programs,  neighborhood  graffiti
abatement  programs,  after school  and park and recreation  programs,  and senior  services.

As proposed,  the voters  of the City  of South Gate will  be asked to approve  a UUT.  The revenue
raised would,  legally,  be required  to be used in the City  of South Gate and could not be taken away
by the County  or the state. Therevenue  collected  will  be sufficientto  eliminate  the structural  deficit
and to maintain  and improve  vital  City  services.  Without  new revenue,  the City  will  be forced  to
reduce essential  community  services  beginning  in the next fiscal year.

Required  Council  Actions
The City  Council  is being  presented  with  all the required  resolutions  for action.  The resolution
declaring  a fiscal  emergency  will  require  a unanimous  vote of tlie City  Council.  The resolution
that  calls for a special  municipal  election,  approve  the ballot  question  with  a directive  for the City
Attorney  to prepare  an impartial  analysis,  and provide  support  and opposition  arguments  and
rebuttals  for the Electiori  ballot  requires  a 4/5'h super majority  vote of the City  Council.

The legal deadline  to place  a ballot  measure  on the June 2, 2026 election  ballot  is March  6, 2026.
A decision  now helps to ensure that all informational  materials  can be disseminated  to the voters
in a timely  fashion  and that there is ample time for the request  and collection  of absentee ballots.

BACKGROUND:
The City's  Current  Budget  Challenge
The City  is facing  a structural  budget  deficit,  meaning  the ongoing  cost of delivering  essential,
municipal  and utility  services  is higher  than the revenue  the City receives.  This deficit  is not a one-
time issue; it is ongoing  and long-term  and will  continue  to grow unless  action  is taken.  Without
new, reliable  funding,  tlie City  will  eventually  be unable  to maintain  current  service  levels.

Why  a Utility  Users  Tax  (UUT)?
A UUT  would  provide  a stable, dedicated  general  fund revenue  source to provide  fiinds  to pay for
City services.  All surrounding  south Los Angeles  cities have an active Utility  Users Tax to provide
significant  general  fund revenue.  South Gate has never had a Utility  Users Tax to provide  revertue
for general  fund services.

If a UUT  measure  was passed in South Gate, the budget  deficit  would  be fixed  and current  service
levels would  be maintained.  This  funding  would  help close the structural  gap and ensure the City
 can maintain  police,  parks and recreation,  community  development,  and public  works  services  for
the community.

  3

  12
 Benefits  to Residents
A UUT helps the City avoid significant  service reductions in the future. These services  include
Police 911 response, school crossing @iards, parks and recreation facilities and programs, special
events, planning, building and code enforcement services, and public works services. The UUT
also supports long-ten'n financial stability and responsible management of community resources.

The  Cost  of Doing  Nothing
Without  a new revenue  source,  the City  will  need to consider:
  *  Cutting service levels, including municipal and infrastructure  services.  The presentation
  that will be provided outlines the scope of the projected  budget  cuts to service  and the
  impacts  these will  have  on the community
  *  Delaying  maintenance  or upgrades,  whicli  can increase  long-teim  costs.
  *  Using  emergency  however, the City currently has a minitum
  reserves,  amount of reserves
  that meet industry standards for fiscal liealtli. Drawing down these reserves any further will
  not be sustainable  or fiscally  responsible.

The  UUT  is a proactive  measure  that  allows  tl"ie City  to stabilize  its budget,  protect  essential
services,  and plan  responsibly  for the future.  The UUT  also provides  a funding  stream  to preserve
vital  City  services.

MAINTENANCE  DISTRICT  N0.  1

PURPOSE:  Annually,  the City  Council  undertakes  certain  proceedings  to levy  and collect
assessments within  the Street Lighting  and Landscape  Maintenance  District  No. 1 ("District").
The first of the actions is to adopt a Resolution  to initiate  the annual proceedings  and order the
preparation of the Engineer's Report.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  initiating
the annual proceedings  for the levy  of the Fiscal  Year  2026/27  assessments  and ordering  the
preparation  of an Engineer's  Report  for  the Street  Lighting  and Landscaping  Maintenance
District No. 1.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The cost of preparing  the Engineer's Report is $8,307 and it will be
funded with Street  Lighting  and Landscaping  Funds budgeted in the Fiscal Year 2026/27
Municipal  Budget.

ANALYSIS:  The  assessment  rate is set at $2.38  per adjusted  front  footage.  Although  the
revenue  from  this  assessment  has remained  the same for  nearly  three  decades,  the cost of
maintaining  the District  has risen, creating  a 'funding  shortfall.  For FY 2026/27,  the revenue  is
estimated  at $1,994,154,  while  maintenance  costs are estimated  at $3,041,636,  resulting  in a
budget  deficit  of $1,184,010.  which  is planned  to be funded  with  restricted  funds  including
Measure  R, Gas Tax and Proposition  A.  This amount  includes  $136,528  for the maintenance  of
the landscaped medians on Long  Beach Blvd  and Garfield  Avenue  recently  constructed,  which
amount added to the deficit.

In April  2016, the City  Council  authorized  an analysis  to explore  ways to address the funding
shortfall,  including  the possibility  of raising  the assessment  rate through  a Proposition  218
process, which  requires  property  owner  approval  for any new or increased  assessments.  At that
time, the consultant  found that while  raising  the rate in the existing  District  could help, creating

  1

  43
 new districts  would  be a more  effective  way to generate  additional  fiinds,  and staff did not move
forward  with  a Proposition  218 effort.

BACKGROTJND:  The District  was established  in 1981  and operates  under  the Landscaping
and  Lighting  Act  of  1972  (California  Streets  and  Highways  Code).  This  law  provides  the
authority  to levy  an assessment  of properties  that receive  a direct  "special  benefit"  from  public
improvements,  such as landscaping  and street lighting.  Since the District  covers  the entire  City,
the assessment  is levied  on all properties  throughout  the City.

To remain  compliance  with  the rules of the district,  District  revenue  can only be used to maintain
and  operate  landscaping  and lighting  systems  throughout  the  City  and  on City  streets.  This
includes  expenses  for  landscaping  (trees,  shrubs,  grass,  irrigation,  and drainage)  and lighting
systems  (streetlights,  decorative  fixtures,  traffic  signals,  and related  equipment),  including  labor
and materials.

Annually,  the District's  funds  are levied  and collected  by the Los  Angeles  County  ASsessor's
Office  ("LA  County")  on behalf  of the City,  in the property  tax roll.  Several  actions  from  the
City  Council  are required  to provide  LA  County  with  the  authority  to levy  and  collect  the
assessments,  according  to LA  County  requirements  and applicable  state law.  The first  step is to
adopt  the proposed  Resolution  which  initiates  the proceedings  and orders  the preparation  of the
Engineer's  Report.

The schedule  for the proceedings  is as follows:

An  Assessment  District  allows  the City  to charge  a fee (assessment)  to properties  that benefit
from  public  improvements,  such  as enhanced  landscaping  and  street  lighting.  These  public
improvements  are considered  a special  benefit  to adjacent  properties.  Funding  for maintenance
and services  comes  from  the annual  assessments  paid by property  owners  within  the District.  To
continue  collecting  these  assessments  for  FY  2026/27,  the  City  must  prepare  an Engineer's
Report  annually  and hold  a public  hearing,  as required  by the Landscaping  and Lighting  Act  of

SUBJECT:  CERTIFICATION  6F  CALPERS  INDUSTRIAL  DISABILITY  RETIREMENT
OF ISMAEL  VERVERA,  A RETIRED  POLICE  SERGEANT

PURPOSE:  To  request  City  Council  adoption  of  a Resolution  certifying  an Industrial  Disability
Retirement  ("IDR")  for  Ismael  Ververa  ("Employee"),  a retired  Police  Seargent  with  South  Gate
Police  Department,  pursuant  to the  California  Government  Code  and California  Public  Employee
Retirement  System  ("CalPERS")  requirements.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  It  is  recommended  that  the  City  Council  adopt  the  attached
Resolution  certifying  that:  a) Employee  is substantially  incapacitated  from  the performance  of the
essential  duties  of his position;  b) Employee's  incapacity  is a result  of industrial  (work-related)  causes;
c) Employee  is eligible  to receive  Industrial  Disability  Retirement  ("IDR")  benefits  through  CalPERS;
and d) The City is not contesting  the medical  determination  of industrial  disability.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no direct  General  Fund  impact.  CalPERS  will  calculate  and administer
the retirement  benefit  directly  based on the employee's  membership  category  and service  credit.

BACKGROUND:  California Government Code F> 21156 sets forth the criteria for the City Council to
make a determination  that a public  employee  is substantially  incapacitated  physically  and/or  mentally
for  the performance  of his  duties  and it thus  eligible  to retire  based  on said  disabling  condition.
CalPERS  requires  City  Council  to adopt a Resolution  certifying  that an employee  is, in fact, eligible  to
receive  IDR benefits.

Employee,  a retired  Police  Sergeant,  was employed  with  the City  of South  Gate from  November  15,
1992,  through  July 17, 2025,  the official  date of his retirement.  On September  14, 2023,  he sustained
an industrial  injury  for  which  he filed  a workers'  compensation  claim.  Subsequently,  Sgt. Ververa
sustained  a second  industrial  injury  on  September  3,  2024,  which  also  resulted  in  a workers'
compensation  claim.  Both  workers'  compensation  claims  remain  pending;  however,  both  have been
accepted.  On June 3, 2025,  Employee  filed  an application  for  an IDR  with  CalPERS.  The basis  of
Employee's  application  for the IDR  benefits  is that the injuries  he sustained  were  in the line  of duty
and have rendered  him  substantially  incapacitated  to perform  his duties  as a sworn  Police  Sergeant.
The  City  then  serit  Employee  to  a competent,  independent  medical  practitioner,  who  examined
Employee  and confirmed  that his condition  was sustained  while  in the line  of duty  with  the City  as a
Police  Sergeant  and that  such injuries  have  rendered  him  substantially  incapacitated  to perform  his

 duties as a Police Sergeant. Accordingly,  it can be concluded  that Ververa  is substantially  incapacitated
within  the meaning  of the California  Government  Code and the Public  Employees'  Retirement  Law
("PERL")  for the performance  of his usual and customer  duties in the position  of Police Sergeant,

Based on the medical evidence, staff recommends that the City Council adopt a Resolution,  which will

SUBJECT:  PROPOSALS  FOR  ON-CALL  PLANNING,  LANDSCAPING,
ENVIRONMENTAL,  AND ECONOMIC  DEVELOPMENT  CONSULTING  SERVICES

PURPOSE:  To provide a list of qualified firms to provide on-call consulting services  for various
planning, landscaping, environmental, and economic  development issues, including:

  *  Planning, zoning, and land use services
  *  Landscape plan review for compliance  with the water efficient  landscape ordinance
  *  Environmental services in compliance  with the California  Environmental  Quality  Act
  (CEQA) and/or National Environmental  Policy Act (NEPA)
  @  Economic  development  advisory services

On-call consulting services are needed to support the City with future development projects, and
economic development efforts including, but not limited to, general plan amendments, code
amendments, rezoning, tentative subdivision maps, conditional use permits, design reviews, plan
reviews, specific plans, environmental services, and economic development.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider adopting a list of qualified
consultants that staff can select from an as-needed basis to provide various services for planning,
landscaping, environmental, and economic  development issues.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no fiscal impact from the establishment of this list, as this list of
consultants does not authorize any scope of work. All work authorized would be project-specific
and would be the responsibility of the applicant unless a project is City-initiated, in which case the
City  would  pay costs.

ANALYSIS:  The City last updated its list of environmental consultants in June 2022, in wich  it
entered into three contracts for on-call consulting services with De Novo Planning Group, EcoTierra
Consulting, and Kimley Horn - referred to as "bench" consultants. Those contracts were extended
until June 28, 2026. The City is now seeking to establish a broader bench list that includes those
three firms plus other qualified environmental  consultants, and expand the list to include  other
disciplines,  including  planning,  economic development,  and landscaping  services.  Selected

  1

  51
 consultants  are not required  to cover  all disciplines,  but may offer  services  for one or more based on
their  areas of expertise.  The expanded  bench  list will  provide  staff more  of a range  of professional
services,  expertise,  pricing,  and availability.

Background
In previous  years,  applicants  requiring  environmental  services  undertook  the primary  studies  with
their  own consultants  and the City  would  peer review  those studies  for reasonableness,  which  is a
legally  acceptable  format.  However,  to ensure  community  interests  are fully  considered  and that
there is an independence  to the analysis  undertaken,  in 2022, the City decided  to prepare  all technical
studies,  initial  studies,  and other dociunents  through  its own qualified  consultants.  All  costs for the
technical  studies,  initial  studies,  and other  documents  were fully  paid through  deposits  required  of
the applicant  at the time  a development  application  is submitted.

Request  for Qualifications
On September  4, 2025,  the City  Council  authorized  the release  of a request  for proposal  (RFQ)  to
solicit  qualified  firms  to submit  proposals  for  on-call  planning,  landscaping,  environmental,  and
economic  development  consulting  services.  The RFQ would  assist in developing  apre-screened  pool
of qualified  consultants  to be able to respond  in a timely  manner  to development  applications.  The
RFQ was sent to 26 consulting  firms  that cover a variety  of services.  Staff received  10 statements  of
qualifications  (SOQs)  in response,  and a correspondence  from  EcoTierra  indicating  they would  like
to remain  on the bench  list  and provide  the same environmental  service.  The two  other  existing
bench  consultants  - Kimley-Horn  and De Novo  Planning  Group  - submitted  an SOQ  to provide
planning  services  while  continuing  to provide  environmental  services.

Establishing  a Consultant  Bench

and  consultant  capabilities.  After  reviewing  responses  and  comrnunicating  with  qualified
consultants,  staff recornrnends  that the City  Council  adopt the following  list of consultants  to provide
services  in their  field  of expertise:

In total, the City would expand its bench of three environmental  consultants to:

  *  8 Planning, zoning, and land use consultants
  *  7 Environmental  consultants
  *  3 Landscape consultants
  *  2 Economic  development  consultants

Once the list of bench consultants is established, projects that require specialized review  as
determined by staff will be sent to consultants based on their field of expertise through a request for
proposal (RFP). An RFP for a project that is not exempt from CEQA may be sent to environmental
consultants for preparation of a CEQA document. Similarly, an RFP for a large project that requires
a complex zone change and General Plan amendment may be sent to planning consultants,
environmental  consultants, and landscape consultants. Proposals received will be reviewed and
vetted before selections are made and contracts are executed. Applicants will be responsible  for
paying for the cost of the City's consultants, plus a 25% administrative  fee.

Planning  Services

Consultants will be contacted if an applicant requests an update to the General Plan, zoning  code,
specific plan, or other long-range planning document. Consultants will need to provide services  on
an as-needed basis, and may be asked to present workshops and training sessions with the Planning
Cornrnission and/or City Council. For applicant-initiated  projects, the applicant is responsible for
submitting a deposit, plus a 25% administrative fee, to cover costs. For City-initiated  projects,  the
City would cover the consultant's costs.

 Additionally,  several  consultants  from  the proposed  qualified  list provide  staff augmentation  in the
event the City  requires  assistance  with  processing  current  plaru'iing  projects.

Environmental  Services
Consultants  will  be responsible  for  the  preparation  of  Environmental  Impact  Reports  (EIR),
Environmental  Impact  Statements  (EIS),  Negative  Declarations,  Mitigated  Negative  Declarations,
technical  studies  and other  CEQA  and National  Environmental  Policy  Act  (NEPA)  documentation
for proposed  projects.  The City  currently  has three  bench  consultants  that provide  environmental
services  and is looking  to expand  the list of qualified  consultants.  In the event  an applicant  wishes
to use its own consultant,  the City  could  use a bench  consultant  to peer review  the work.

Landscaping  Services
The City  of South  Gate has a Water  Conservation  Ordinance  adopted  in 2009 that promotes  water
conservation  measures  but may not fiilly  meet new State standards.  If the City  decides  to update  its
ordinance,  a consultant  can be selected  from  the bench  list to prepare  an ordinance  amendment,
which  would  be paid  for by the City.  For large private  development,  landscape  consultants  could
review  the  landscape  plan  for  compliance.  Historically,  staff  has  reviewed  landscape  plans.
Applicants  would  cover the cost if a landscape  consultant  is needed.

Economic  Development  Services
Economic  development  consultants  will  provide  advisory  services  on  economic  development.
Occasionally,  the City  requires  economic  development  data and analysis  for decision-makers  and
requires  a consultant  that specializes  in economics  and market  conditions.  The City seeks consultants
who  can provide  these  services  on an as-needed  basis.  Consultants  may  be asked  to present
workshops  and training  sessions  with  the Planning  Commission  and/or  City  Council.  The City  will
pay for city-initiated  projects.

CONCLUSION:  The expanded  list of bench  consultants  will  assist staff  in making  selections  to
serve as an extension  of staff.  Consultants  are specialized  in their field  of expertise  and can alleviate
the workload  placed  on regular  staff.  This  improves  customer  service  and ensures  that projects  are
thoroughly  reviewed  for compliance  with  state and federal  laws. In the event an applicant  wishes  to
use its own consultant,  the City  could  use a bench  consultant  to peer review  the work.

If the bench  list is acceptable  to City  Council,  staff  will  use the list  when  development  projects
warrant  the need  for  a consultant  or consultant  services  are needed  for  a City-initiated  project.
Contracts  with  the consultants  will  be executed  at a later  time  when  a development  project  is
submitted  or services  are needed.

Planning  Consultants
The City occasionally  requires  updates  to its General  Plan, zoning  code, specific  plans, and other  planning
documents.  The City seeks consultants  who  can provide  these  planning  services  on an as-needed  basis.
Consultants  may be asked  to present  workshops  and training  sessions  with  the  Planning  Commission
and/or City Council.

Environmental  Consultants
The State of California  has an environmental  statute  called  California  Environmental  Quality  Act (CEQA).
The National  Environmental  Policy  Act (NEPA) is a United  States  Environmental  law that  promotes  the
enhancement  of the  environment  and  established  the  President's  Council  on Environmental  Quality
(CEQ). Both laws require  state  and local agencies  to identify  the significant  environmental  impacts  of their
actions  and avoid or mitigate  those  impacts,  if feasible.

The consultant(s)  selected  will be responsible  for the preparation  of Environmental  Impact  Reports  (EIR),
Environmental  Impact  Statements  (ELS), Negative  Declarations,  Mitigated  Negative  Declarations,  technical
studies  and other  California  Environmental  Quality  Act (CEQA)  and National  Environmental  Policy  Act
(NEPA) documentation  for  proposed projects.  The  consultant/s will be willing to work collaboratively  with,
and manage  the work  of, other  members  of the environmental  analysis  team.

The City  of South  Gate  has a Water  Conservation  Ordinance  adopted  in 2009  that  promotes  water
conservation  measures  but may not fully  meet the requirements  of MWELO.  Thus, the City must  rely and
implement  the State's  MWELO.

 The  City  is seeking  guidance  from  landscape  consultants  on  adopting  a local  WELO  or continuing

implementing  the standards  in the State MWELO.  Furthermore,  the City is seeking  consultants  to review

plans  for  MWELO  compliance,  which  includes  but is not  limited  to reviewing  landscape  and irrigation

plans,  providing  recommendations  on improving  water  efficiency  measures,  conducting  compliance

inspections,  and finalizing  permits.

Economic  Development  Consultants

City requires  economic  development  data for decision-makers  and requires  a consultant  that  specializes

in economics  and market  conditions.  The City seeks consultants  who can provide  these  services  on an as-

needed  basis. Consultants  may be asked to present  workshops  and training  sessions  with  the  Planning

Commission  and/or City Council.

  2. Work  Plan

  2.a  Methodology

  2.a. 1 Advance  Planning
  Willdan's  planners  have expertise  with general  plans; area and specific  plans; zoning  codes, housing  elements;
  community  plans; transportation  plans, historic  resource  plans; climate  action  plans; infill development;  and city
  annexations.  Upon receiving  an advance  planning  assignment,  we will assign expert  staff, discuss the project's  goals
  and objectives  with City staff,  coordinate  with staff and stakeholders,  prepare  relevant  reports,  policy  documents  and
  presentations;  regularly  update  staff on progress,  and attend  City Planning  Commission  and Council  meetings.

  2.C1.2  Entitlement  Processing
  Willdan's  planners  are conscientious  about  meeting  timeframe  requirements  for the Permit  Streamlining  Act,
  Mitigation  Fee Act, Subdivision  Map Act, and shot-clock  deadlines  of the federal 1996 Telecommunications  Act. Upon
  receiving  an application  for processing,  we will assign the appropriate  case planner  to the project,  who will function  as
  part of the City's development  review  team. The case planner  will review  the application  for completeness  and inform
  the applicant  of any outstanding  items required  for processing.  We follow  our clients'  procedures  for routing  the
  application  to the development  review  team,  and maintain  communication  with the applicant.  Finally,  the case
  planner  will prepare  staff reports,  conditions  of approval,  and resolutions  for the designated  hearing  bodies,  and
  present  the project  if so directed.

  2.a.3  Environmental  Review
  Willdan  routinely  prepares  CEQA and NEPA environmental  documentation  for public  and discretionary  private
  projects,  such as general  plan amendments,  code amendments,  rezones,  tentative  subdivision  maps, conditional  use
  permits,  design reviews,  specific  plans, and infrastructure  improvements.

  Upon receiving  an assignment  for environmental  review,  we will assign the appropriate  envircnmental  planner  to the
  project,  who will screen the project  for exemptions  and determine  the level of documentation  required.  For projects
  subject  to CEQA, an Initial Study will be prepared,  following  the CEQA Guidelines  Appendix  G (or other  checklists  for
  infill projects).  Alternatively,  a memo documenting  the project's  eligibility  for a Categorical  Exemption  will be
  prepared.  Willdan"s  in-house  engineers  prepare  transportation  analyses  (vehicle  miles traveled)  and geotechnical
  studies.  Our subject-matter  consultant,  Rincon Consultants,  Inc., assists with  other technical  studies,  such as cultural
  or biological  resources,  noise and vibration,  or arboricultural  reports.  The environmental  planner  will submit  a
  screencheck  draft  of the Initial  Study or CE memorandum  for City staff review,  and revise the document(s)  accordingly
  prior to preparing  them for public review.

  The environmental  planner  will prepare  all required  notices,  such as a Notice  oflntent  to Adopt  a Negative
  Declaration,  Notice  of Availability  of an Environmental  Impact  Report,  and a Notice  of Completion.  With the City's
  permission,  all documentation  will be uploaded  to the State Clearinghouse  CEQAnet  database.  After  public circulation
  and receipt  of comments  on the draft  environmental  document,  the environmental  planner  will prepare  detailed
  written  responses,  a mitigation  monitoring  and reporting  program,  and the final environmental  document.

  For projects  subject  to NEPA, typically  infrastructure  projects  funded  through  Caltrans  or HUD Community
  Development  Block Grants,  the environmental  planner  will assemble  the required  exhibits  for completing  a PES Form
  6a or Part 58 review  and submit  them through  the City's project  manager  to Caltrans  or HUD. Follow-up  technical
  studies  or memoranda  will either  be prepared  by Rincon or Willdan  in-house  staff. The federal  agency will determine
  whether  further  environmental  documentation,  such as an Environmental  Assessment  (EA) or an Environmental
  Impact  Statement  (ELS) will be required,  resulting  in publication  of a Finding  of No Significant  Effect (FONSI) or a
  Record of Decision  (ROD) in the Federal  Register.  Typically,  however,  most projects  undertaken  by cities that are
  federally  funded  are categorically  excluded  from detailed  environmental  analysis,  simplifying  the documentation.

  2.a.4 Water Conservation  Ordinance  Update/Landscape  Plan Review
  Willdan's  landscapearchitect team will meet with City staff. Willdan will review the City's current Water Conservation
  Ordinance  and recommend  updates to conform to the current State mandated  Model Water Efficient Landscape
  Ordinance  (MWELO). Willdan will review landscape plans associated with entitlement  applications  within two to three
  weeks after receipt from the City, and will allow for a minimum of two revision cycles. Landscape plan review includes
  reviewing construction  plans, irrigation plans, planting plans, and landscape construction  details. Willdan can inspect
  landscape construction  compliance, including MWELO-compliant irrigation installation.

  2.a.5  Financial  Services
  Willdan  Financial Services, a subsidiary  of Willdan Group, Inc., provides numerous  services to our municipal  clients.
  These services include assessment district administration,  cost allocation  studies, development  impact fee studies,
  fiscal impact analyses, utility rate analyses, and arbitrage/rebate  services. Recently, Willdan  Financial Services has
  completed a development impact fee analysis for the City of Artesia, and will be preparing an in-lieu affordable
  housing fee study for Artesia's new Mixed-Use Overlay ordinance.

  2.b Project  Schedule
  To meet the City"s performance  expectations  and deadlines, Willdan's  planners maintain  project logs that track each
  project's milestones and deliverables through the environmental and entitlement review process. Scheduling alerts
  will be set up using Microsoft Outlook" Calendar for important deadlines. While not all projects can meet strict
  processing deadlines  due to complex issues that might require an approval or information  from an outside  agency,
  Willdan"s planners proactively  resolve project challenges so that they can quickly be presented to the City Planning
  Commission  and City Council. At all times, Willdan planners regularly inform our clients' about progress.

  Processing times vary depending on the project. Many advance planning projects require multiple years to complete
  to allow for sufficient time for public outreach and policy development. Entitlement applications can also range from
  months to years, depending on the size and complexity of the project and the applicant's cooperation in responding to
  City requirements. A typical Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration requires from four to six months, and an
  Environmental  Impact Report can take one year from intake to certification.

PURPOSE:  Tetra  Tech  was  awarded  Contract  No.  2024-65-CC  to  prepare  the  design  and
constniction  documents  for the South Gate Park PFAS  Treatment  Plant Project  (PFAS  Treatment
Project).  Since the contract  was awarded, additional  improvements  have been identified  to enhance the
design  and performance  of the treatment  system,  as well  as to accommodate  construction  of the
facility.  These improvements  require the removal  of existing  structures within  the project  footprint  and
the design of replacement facilities. Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. 2024-65-CC provides the
additional  design services necessary to complete  this work.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No.  2024-63-CC with Tetra Tech to provide

  b.  Appropriating  $150,000  in Water Funds to fully  fund the design phase on the PFAS Treatment
  Project;
  c.  Authorizing  the City Manager  to approve  and execute amendments  up to a cumulative  amount

  d.  Authorizing the Mayor to execute Amendment  No. 2 to Contract  No. 2024-65-CC  in a form

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund.  Amendment  No. 2 is in the amount of

to fully fund the design phase, for a graqd total appropriation of $1,050,000.

 ANALYSIS:  Since  the  original  design  contract  was  awarded,  additional  site,  operational,  and
constructability  needs have been identified  that are necessary  to complete  a compliant  and buildable
PFAS  Treatment  Plant  at South  Gate Park. As the design  progressed,  it became  clear that the footprint
of the treatment  system  and associated  piping  will  require  removal  of an existing  hut  and the old
storage  building  located  within  the  project  area.  Additional  design  work  is  needed  to  prepare
demolition  plans and to design  a replacement  storage  facility  to maintain  ongoing  operational  needs.

Further  refinements  are also required  to improve  system  performance  and operational  flexibility.  These
include  design  of a bypass  line  to allow  continued  operation  during  maintenance,  incorporation  of
automatic  flush  valves  to improve  well  operations,  and expansion  of the design  to connect  Well  13 to
the PFAS  treatment  system.  These  elements  are necessary  to ensure  the system  operates  reliably  and
efficiently  once constnicted.

Amendment  No.  2 provides  $142,500  to incorporate  the additional  design  services  needed  to address
these sites, operational,  and constructability  requirements,  complete  the project  design,  and ensure  the
PFAS  Treatment  Plant  can be constructed  and operated  in compliance  with  regulatory  standards  while
maintaining  the project  schedule.

BACKGROUND:  The City  relies  on groundwater  from  the Central  Basin  aquifers  to supply  drinking
water  to the  community.  Eight  City-owned  water  wells  pump  groundwater  into  the  City's  water
distribution  system.  In recent  years,  per- and polyfluoroalkyl  substances  (PFAS)  have been detected  in
the groundwater  at these well  sites.  As a precautionary  measure  to protect  public  health,  the Public
Works  Department  temporarily  shut down  water production  at the affected  wells.

In April  2024, the U.S. Environmental  Protection  Agency  (EPA)  adopted  final  Maximum  Contaminant
Levels  (MCLs)  for PFAS,  which  became  effective  on June 25, 2024.  The new standards  set very  low
allowable  limits  for PFOA  and PFOS  at 4.O nanograms  per liter.  While  compliance  monitoring  begins
in 2027 and enforcement  will  not occur  until  2029,  these regulations  establish  the design  requirements
for 'future  treatment  facilities.  Based  on detected  PFAS  levels,  the City  must  design  and construct  a
PFAS  treatment  system  to meet  State and federal  drinking  water  standards  and restore  'full use of the
affected  wells.

On August  13, 2024,  the City  Council  awarded  a design  services  contract  to Tetra  Tech  in the amount
of $775,000  to prepare  plans and specifications  for the South  Gate Park PFAS  Treatment  Plant Project.
Amendment  No.  1, in the amount  of $45,995,  was subsequently  approved  to complete  additional  site
surveying,  relocate  the treatment  plant,  and design  a bypass  line.

The Public  Works  Department  is now  recommending  approval  of Amendment  No.  2 to complete  the
remaining  design  work  necessary  for the PFAS  treatment  system  serving  the South  Gate Park  water
wells.

Final  design  of the project  is anticipated  to be completed  in June 2026.

SUBJECT:  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  WITH  INTERWEST
CONSULTING  GROUP,  INC.  FOR  CONSTRUCTION  INSPECTION  SERVICES  FOR
THE  SOUTH  GATE  POLICE  DEPARTMENT'S  (SGPD)  HEATING,  VENTILLATION
AND  AIR  CONDITIONING  (HVAC)  REPLACEMENT,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.  667-GEN

PURPOSE:  The  South  Gate  Police  Department  Detention  Center  is currently  served  by an
outdated  air-handling  system  that lacks  air conditioning.  The HVAC  Replacement  Project  will
resolve  this  issue  and provide  reliable  heating  and cooling.  Design  is now  complete  and the
project  is moving  into  the construction  phase.  The  proposed  agreement  authorizes  Interwest
Consulting  Group  to provide  inspections  services  during  construction.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  Interwest  Consulting  Group,  Inc.,  to provide  inspection
  services  for  the construction  of the SGPD  HVAC  Replacement,  City  Project  No.  667-
  GEN,  in an amount  not to exceed  $84,000; and
  b.  Authorize  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The Agreement  is in the amount  of $84,000,  and it will  be funded  with
Building  Infrastructure  &  Maintenance  (BIM)  Funds  budgeted  in  the  Fiscal  Year  2025/26
Capital  Improvement  Program.  The HVAC  Project  is budgeted  with  $1.2 Million  in BIM  Funds.

ANALYSIS:  The Public  Works  Department  issued  a Request  for Proposal  (RFP)  to the City's
On-Call  Engineering  firms  to  procure  construction  inspection  services  for  the  HVAC
Replacement  Project  at the South  Gate  Police  Department  Detention  Center.  Of the three  (3)
firms  invited,  only  Interwest  Consulting  Group,  Inc. submitted  a proposal.

Staff  reviewed  the  proposed  fee  and  determined  that  the  cost  is reasonable,  consistent  with
industt7-standard pricing for specialized mechanical construction inspection, and acceptable
based on the anticipated  level  of effort  and duration  of the project.

Based  on Interwest's  qualifications,  proposed  scope,  and compliance  with  the RFP,  staff  has
determined  that  the  firm  is well-qualified  to  provide  the  required  services.  Therefore,  staff
recornrnends  awarding  the construction  inspection  agreement  to Interwest  Consulting  Group,
Inc.

  1

  554
 BACKGROUND:  The  South  Gate Police  Department  Detention  Center  is currently  equipped
with  an aging  air-handling  system  that provides  warm  air through  the existing  boiler  unit  and
relies  on unconditioned  outside  air for ventilation.  The system  does not provide  air conditioning.
During  the sutnmer  months,  indoor  temperatures  within  the Detention  Center  can exceed  80
degrees,  creating  uncomfortable  working  conditions  for staff and resulting  in frequent  complaints
from  inmates.  The  current  system  has also  become  increasingly  difficult  to maintain  due to
outdated  components  and limited  availability  of replacement  parts.

The HVAC  Project  is included  in the Fiscal  Year  2025/26  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The
purpose  of the project  is to replace  the existing  air-handling  unit  with  a new,  energy-efficient
HVAC  system  capable  of providing  both  heating  and cooling  as needed  to maintain  proper  air
circulation,  temperature,  and comfort  levels  within  the Detention  Center.  The  scope  of work
includes  the removal  and replacement  of the existing  system,  installation  of new  ductwork  and
controls,  and associated  electrical,  mechanical,  and plumbing  improvements.  Renovation  of other
areas  within  the  South  Gate  Police  Station  will  be addressed  in  a future  phase  as funding
becomes  available.

The  proposed  fee is $84,000.  The  scope  of work  includes,  but  is not  limited  to, providing
construction  inspection  services  with  daily  reporting;  reviewing  construction  quantities;
evaluating  potential  change  orders;  reviewing  and verifying  contractor-submitted  invoices;  and
ensuring  overall  compliance  with  approved  plans,  specifications,  and contract  requirements.

Construction  is planned  to start January  2026 and be completed  within  124 working  days.

BACKGROUND:  The  South  Gate  Police  Station,  constructed  in 1948,  currently  houses  the
City's  Emergency  Operations  Center  ("EOC")  in a subterranean  portion  of the building.  This
location  has proven  to be unsuitable  for modern  emergency  response  needs.  It is susceptible  &
vulnerable  to flooding,  is not fully  accessible  to individuals  with  disabilities,  and experiences
comi'nunication  challenges  due to thick  concrete  walls.  Because  clear and reliable  comi'nunication
is essential  during  emergencies,  the City  has determined  that relocating  the EOC  is necessary  to
ensure effective  response  during  major  events.

This  project  proposes  relocating  the existing  EOC  from  the SGPD  basement  to a new  facility
within  the Civic  Center  by repurposing  a portion  of the museum  to meet modern  EOC  standards.
The reconfigured  space is designed  to serve multi-purpose  functions,  it will  operate  as an EOC  on
an as-needed  basis  and, during  normal  operations,  function  as a conference  room,  community
meeting  space, and museum  area. When  the EOC is activated,  the space will  be closed to the public
and fully  dedicated  to emergency  operations.  The City  is committed  to preserving  the museum
experience.  Some exhibits  currently  located  in the repurposed  area will  be relocated  to the eastern
side ofthe  museum  and will  remain  available  for public  viewing  whenever  possible.  Other exhibits
will  be incorporated  into the redesigned  space so that elements  of the museum  remain  visible  while
allowing  adequate  room  for emergency  operations.

in  a subterranean  section  of the building.This  location  is prone to flooding,  lacks ADA-compliant  access, and faces
significant  communication  challenges  due to the thick  concrete  walls. Given that effective  communication  is critical

SCOPE  OF SERVICES
We understand  that the scope of work  requested  in this RFP is the preparation  of the full set of construction
documents  necessary  to bid and construct  the project.  This includes  the preparation  of the Plans, Specifications
and Engineer's  Estimates,  obtaining  any permits  required  for the project  such as building  permits,  utility  permits,  etc.
and clearances.

We understand  that this project  RFP explicitly  requires  that the space within  the building  be designed  and
constructed  to meet  Essential  Facility standards,  including  Risk Category  IV structural  criteria  to ensure  life safety
and continued  operation  during  extreme  events, redundant  power  systems with  appropriately  sized UPS and
backup generator  capacity  to support  critical  functions  without  interruption,  HVAC  systems with  emergency
pressiirization  and filtration  to maintain  air quality, pressure  differentials,  and occupant  protection  during  hazardous
conditions,  and resilient  ICT and AV infrastructure  capable of supporting  secure, 24/7 communications,  data
management,  and situational  awareness  during  EOC activation.

 We also understand that during non-emergency periods, the designated space functions as part of the museum,
serving educational and public engagement purposes. Upon activation, the area must be rapidly converted  into
a fully operational Emergency Operations Center (EOC), typically within a few hours.This requires a flexible
layout with modular furnishings and quickly deployable equipment that allows the space to transition  efficiently
from its public use to an emergency command environment.All critical infrastructure, including power, HVAC,
communications, and audiovisual systems-must remain in a ready state at all times, designed to support
continuous operation during emergencies. Lighting controls must support both museum and EOC functions, with
programmable scenes,task-specific illumination, and emergency lighting modes to ensure visibility, comfort, and
energy efficiency under varying operational conditions.Access to the space will shift from public to restricted,
requiring secure entry and separation from surrounding uses. Storage for emergency equipment and supplies
must be integrated into the design to support rapid deployment, while adjacent facilities must support round-the-
clock occupancy by EOC personnel. Overall, the dual-use design must balance public-facing functionality  with the
resilience, security, and reliability needed for emergency response operations.

The design of the Emergency Operations Center (EOC) will adhere to all applicable federal, state, and local
codes and standards, including the International Building Code (IBC) and ASCE 7 for Risk Category IV structural
performance, NFPA 101 and I 10 for life safety and emergency power systems, FEMA guidelines for continuity  and
hazard mitigation, NIST standards for cybersecurity of ICT systems, and, where appropriate,  UFC antiterrorism
standards for enhanced physical protection, while also complying with ADA accessibility,ASHRAE requirements  for
ventilation and energy efficiency, the National Electrical Code (NEC), and all relevant local fire, energy, mechanical,
and plumbing codes to ensure a resilient, secure, and mission-ready  essential facility.

As part of the design services, BOAArchitecture will provide a concept-level floor plan and color renderings to
illustrate the dual-use layout (museum/educational programming vs. EOC activation). BOA will also resolve all the

PROJECT  PROCESS

This project includes our Project Process, which describes our approach and methodology  to a
design and build project. The entire process is made up of four phases in which each one is
built upon the other.

The two phases, Program Phase anrJ Design Phase, will require collaboration  between us
BOA, and the city to define all the project requirements.  Without collaboration,  it is not
possible to define the customer's  objectives  and expectations,  nor design a system that will
meet them

Within both the Program and Design Phase, the client will be required to review and approve
all deliverables before proceeding  to the next phase. This allows the ciient to fully understand
their systems specification, capabilities,  budgets, timelines, etc. This review and approva!
process confirms that the design is meeting their objectives  and expectations.

The Project Process includes value engineering  throughout  the entire process, which allows us
to discuss alternative  designs, products and/or  processes  that could be applied to the project
with the benefit of saving the customer money.

PURPOSE:  The  City's  West  Side  Reservoir  requires  rehabilitation  to improve  reliability,
extend  the facility's  service  life,  and  address  identified  maintenance  needs.  To advance  this
effort,  staff recommend  approving  an agreement  with  Harper  and Associates  Engineering  Inc. on
a sole-source  basis  for  specialty  engineering  design  services  and  amending  the  Capital
Improvement  Program  to include  the West Side Reservoir  Rehabilitation  Project.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Professional  Services  Agreement  with  Harper  & Associates  Engineering,  Inc.,
  to prepare  design  and construction  documents  for the West  Side Reservoir  Rehabilitation
  Project,  City  Project  No. 742-WTR,  in an amount  not to exceed  $48,380;
  b.  Amending  the Fiscal  Year  2025/26  Capital  Improvement  Program  to add the West  Side
  Reservoir  Rehabilitation  Project  and appropriate  $88,380  in Water  Funds  to fully  fund  its
  design  phase;
  c.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to approve  and execute  amendments  as needed to complete
  the design  phase; and
  d.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to  the  City
  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no  impact  to  the  General  Fund.  The  Agreement  amount  of
$48,380  will  be :tunded  by the Water  Fund.  A total  Water  Fund  appropriation  of  $88,380 is
reauired  to fully  fund the design  phase.

ANALYSIS:  The  City's  drinking  water  system  uses several  large  storage  tanks  and keeping
them  in good  condition  is important  for  safe and reliable  water  service.  During  the Hawkins

  1  651
 Reservoir  project,  staff  also inspected  the West  Side Reservoir  tanks  and found  that they  are in
poor  shape. The paint  on the roof  is heavily  rusted,  some metal  has started  to deteriorate,  and the
safety railings  and ladders  need to be updated.  The current  paint  system  is more than 26 years old
and has outlived  its useful  life.

The proposed  $48,380  agreement  will  pay for the engineering  work  needed  to design  the repairs.
This includes  preparing  plans to fix damaged  areas, repaint  the tanks,  and upgrade  safety  features
so the facility  is protected  from  further  damage  and continues  to provide  safe, clean water.  The
cost is considered  good  value  because  it provides  expert  work  now  that can help prevent  more
expensive  problems  in the future.

BACKGROUND:  The  City  owns  and  operates  a municipal  water  system  that  serves
approximately  90%  of residents  and businesses.  The West  Side Reservoir  site, located  at 2750
Tweedy  Boulevard,  includes  two  groundwater  wells  and two  steel  storage  tanks,  each with  a
capacity  of 2.5 million  gallons.  The tanks  were  constructed  in 1999,  are approximately  35 feet
tall  and 94 feet in diameter  and were  originally  coated  with  coal tar enatnel  on the interior  and
epoxy  on the exterior.  The exterior  roof  coating  is now  more  than 25 years  old and has reached
the end of its service  life.

Recent  inspections  performed  as part  of the Hawkins  Reservoir  project  identified  that the roof
coating  on both  tanks  is failing,  with  rust,  areas  of metal  deterioration,  and outdated  safety
railings  and ladders.  Full  rehabilitation,  including  surface  preparation,  new coatings,  patching  of
damaged  areas,  and  safety  upgrades,  is recommended  to  maintain  the  tanks  in  serviceable
condition.

Given  the specialized  nature  of tank  rehabilitation,  staff  requested  a proposal  from  Harper  &
Associates  Engineering  (HAE),  a firm  with  extensive  experience  in coating  systems,  welding,
structural  repairs,  and  water  reservoir  rehabilitation.  HAE  recently  completed  the  Hawkins
Reservoir  Rehabilitation  design,  demonstrating  their  familiarity  with  the  City's  system  and
requirements.  The proposed  Agreement  with  HAE  provides  the following:

@  Qualified  Project  Manager  - Offers  more  than  25 years  of experience  and has expertise
  in  corrosion  and  tank  structural  engineering  projects,  primarily  related  to  steel  and
  concreate  tank rehabilitation.

*  Successful  Track  Record  -  In 1979,  HAE  was  the first  engineering  firm  in  Southern
  California  to provide  full-time  quality  control  coating  and paint  inspection.  HAE  was  a
  member  of the original  committee  that formulated  the National  Association  of Corrosion
  Engineers  (NACE)  coating  inspection  program  and testing.  HAE  inspectors  not only  have
  NACE  certifications  but have  field  experience  in coating  and painting  with  being  either
  past foremen  or superintendents  for coating  contractors.

@  Experience  on  Similar  Projects  -  HAE's  experience  with  tank  coating  projects  spans
  across many  water  purveyors  such as Coachella  Valley  Water  District,  Long  Beach  Water
  Department,  Golden  State Water  Company,  and San Gabriel  Valley  Water  Company.

  ("Willdan")  to provide  these  services  for  the  successful  delivery  of the AMR  Project,  City
  Project  No. 740-WTR.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  Willdan,  Inc.  to perform  construction  management  and
  inspection  services  on the Automatic  Meter  Reading  Upgrade,  Phase V, City  Project  No.
  740-WTR,  in an amount  not-to-exceed  $149,574;
  b.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to approve  and execute  amendments  to the Agreement  up
  to a cumulative  amount  of $50,000  from  Water  Fund;  and
  c.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to the  City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The proposed  Agreement,  totaling
  $149,574,  will  be funded  entirely  with  Water  Funds  budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year  2025/26  Capital
  Improvement  Program.

  ANALYSIS:  Construction  of the AMR  Project  will  begin  soon,  and it will  require  over  850
  hours  of management  and  inspection  effort.  The  Department  of  Public  Works,  Engineering
  Division,  lacks  sufficient  in-house  staff  to provided  the needed  construction  management  and
  inspection  services.  Therefore,  it is recommended  to retain  a construction  management  and
  inspection  services  consultant  to oversee  the work.

  Staff  issued  a Request  for Task  Proposals  ("RFTP")  to the four  consulting  firms  that currentlay
  have  contracts  with  the City  for on-call  engineering  services.  Three  proposals  were  received.

 Willdan was determined to be the highest  qualified  to provide  the services,  with  the proposed
team being  the same group  that  successfully  construction  managed  the previous  project  phase.
That said, staff recomtnends  awarding  the proposed  Agreement  to Willdan.

BACKGROUND:  The City's  water  system  provides  drinking  water  service  to approximately
90 percent of all properties, supported by a network  of over 14,200  water  meters  used to record
consiunption and generate customer billing.

The  Public  Works  Department  is implementing  a multi-phase  program  to upgrade  all  water
meters  to an automated  system,  eliminating  the need  for  manual  reading.  The  AMR  Project
represents  the fifth  phase of this program.  To date, approximately  4,000  automated  meters  have
been installed  for residential  customers  and 500 for commercial  and multi-family  customers.  The
AMR  Project  will  build  on this  progress  by  replacing  an additional  1,659  meters  serving
residential  and cornrnercial  customers  on the west side of the City.

On October  23, 2025,  a RFTP  was issued  to four  (4) engineering  consulting  firms,  and three  (3)
proposals  were received  as summarized  below.

  Consultant  Fee Proposal

  Interwest  $184,600

A selection  committee  consisting  of the City's  Water  Division  Manager  and the Principal  Civil
Engineer  - Water  Resources  Section  Manager  evaluated  all proposals.  Each  consultant  met the
minimum  qualification  criteria,  including  construction  management  experience,  inspection
capabilities,  and labor  compliance  expertise.  However,  Willdan  Engineering  received  the highest
overall  ranking.  The  proposed  construction  manager  and inspector  previously  provided  these
same  services  during  an  earlier  phase  of  the  project,  which  was  completed  successfully,
demonstrating  strong  familiarity  with  the City's  water  system  and project  requirements.  For
these reasons,  Willdan  is recommended  for the contract.  Willdan  provides  the following  benefits
to the project:

  *  Competitive  Fees - The fee proposal  is $149,574  and is competitive,  as it represents  the
  lowest  fee proposal.

  *  Experienced  Construction  Manager  - The Construction  Manager  has over  30 years  of
  experience.

  *  Qualified  Team  and Expertise  - Willdan  provides  a comprehensive  in-house  team with
  the experience,  technical  knowledge,  and professionalism  required  for the AMR  Project.
  Their  staff  includes  licensed  engineers,  construction  and program  managers,  inspectors,
  office  engineers,  technicians,  and  administrative  support  personnel.  The  primary  and
  alternate  inspectors  each have over 30 years of water-industry  experience,  enabling  them
  to perform  inspections,  testing,  and labor  compliance  effectively  and to ensure the project
  is constructed  in accordance  with  the plans and specifications.

  *  Experience  On  Similar  Projects  -  Willdan's  core  specialties  include  construction
  management  and inspection  of Public  Works  projects,  and they have recently  completed

The  scope  of  services  of  the  proposed  Agreement  consists  of  construction  management,
construction  inspection,  and labor  compliance.

Construction  is anticipated  to begin  in April/May  2026  (a:[ter the procurement  of the meters  is
complete)  and be completed  by September  2026.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  GENTRY  GENERAL  ENGINEERING,  INC.,  FOR
THE  CONSTRUCTION  OF  THE  AUTOMATIC  METER  READING  UPGRADE,
PHASE  V, CITY  PROJECT  N0.  7 40-WTR

PURPOSE:  The  City  is implementing  a multi-phase  program  to replace  aging  water  meters
with  Automatic  Meter  Reading  (AMR)  meters  to improve  accuracy  and reduce  manual  meter
reading.  Phase V will  replace  1,659  meters  in Meter  Route  Cycle  4 on the west  side of the City
and is now 'fully  designed,  bid, and ready  for construction.  The purpose  of this action  is to award
a construction  services  agreement  to Gentry  General  Engineering,  Inc.  for  the installation  of
these meters under  City  Project  No. 740-WTR.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Agreement  with  Gentry  General  Engineering,  Inc.,  to replace  1,659  water
  meters  under  the Automatic  Meter  Reading  Upgrade,  Phase  V,  City  Project  No.  740-
  WTR,  in an amount  not-to-exceed  $1,558,203;
  b. Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to  the  City
  Attorney;
  c.  Appropriating  $2,012,649  from  the  Water  Fund  to  fully  fund  the  Automatic  Meter
  Reading  Upgrade,  Phase V, City  Project  No. 740-WTR;
  d.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to approve  and execute  amendments  to the Agreement  up

  to a cumulative  amount  of $100,000  from  Water  Fund;  and
  e.  Approving  the Notice  of Exemption  for the Automatic  Meter  Reading  Upgrade,  Phase V
  City Project  No.  740-WTR.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The project  is budgeted  for
$100,000 in FY 2025/26.  Appropriation  of an additional  $2,012,649  from  the Water  Funds  is
required  to fully  fund the project.  The budget  is surnrnarized  below:

  Water  Funds

  Staff Time/Design  $52,223
  Construction  $1,558,203
  Construction  Contingency  $200,000
  Construction  Management/  Inspection  / Contingency  $200,000

  Total  Budget  $2,112,649

  ANALYSIS:  The  water  system  is equipped  with  more  than  14,300  water  meters.  City  staff
  reads about 2/3rd  of the meters  manually  every  month.  This approach  is inefficient,  outdated  and
  lacks use of available  technology.  The solution  is to automate  the water meters  by replacing  them
  with  AMR  meters.  Amongst  the benefits,  AMR  meters  can be read  automatically  through  a
  handheld  device,  which  reduces  the time  spent  reading  meters  by  50%.  The  AMR  Upgrade
  Project  will  replace  1,659  water  meters  with  AMRs.  The project  is ready for construction.

  The City  Council  should  be aware  that some customers  will  receive  higher  water  bills  after the
  AMR  meters  are installed.  This  is because  the existing  water  meters  have aged and are under-
  recording  the amount  of water  used by customers  by up to 10%.  This issue will  be corrected,  and
  some water  bills  could  increase  by up to 10o/o.

  BACKGROTJND:  The AMR  Project  (Phase  V) is a continuation  of the Phases I, II, III,  and
  IV Project  which  were completed  in 2017,  2018,  2024,  and 2025  respectively.  In Phase I, 2,020
  AMR  Meters  were installed,  where  Phase II, installed  410 AMR  meters,  and an additional  1,725
  meters  replaced  in Phase III.  Phase I and III  focused  on residential  accounts  (meter  sizes %" and
  l "), whereas  Phase II focused  on commercial  and multi-residential  accounts  (meters  sizes %" up
  to 2"). Phase II was needed  to fiilly  automate  Meter  Route  C-2. Phase IV focused  on residential
  accounts  on Meter  Route  C-3. Phase V will  focus  on residential  accounts  on Meter  Route  C-4.

  The AMR  Upgrade  Project  has been  designed,  construction  bids  have  been received,  and the
  proposed  Agreement  is necessary  to start  constniction.  Construction  is anticipated  to begin  in
  April/May  2026 and be completed  by September  2026.

  On October  23, 2025,  staff  advertised  the Notice  Inviting  Bids  in PlanetBids.  The project  was
  also advertised  in the newspaper.  On November  20, 2025,  three bids were received  and opened
  by the City  Clerk  in a public  forum.  The summary  of the bid is as follows:

  Gentry  General  Engineering,  Inc.  submitted  the lowest  responsible  and responsive  bid,  with  a

  Located  in the City  of Colton,  CA,  Gentry  General  Engineering,  Inc.  exhibits  the capability,

  SUBJECT:  PURCHASE  ORDER  FOR  RENEWAL  OF SOFTWARE  MAINTENANCE
  AND  SUPPORT  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  FOR  THE  POLICE  DEPARTMENT

  PURPOSE:  To renew  the existing  contract  with  Hitech  Systems,  Inc. dba Pulsiam  ("Pulsiarn")
  for  maintenance  and  support  services  agreement  which  includes  Computer  Aided  Dispatch
  ("CAD")  and Records  Management  Systems  ("RMS")  for the Police  Department.  South  Gate
  Municipal  Code requires  that all agreements  more than $50,000  be approved  by the City  Council.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  will  consider  authorizing  the issuance  of a
  Purchase  Order with  Pulsiarn  to renew  the Software  Maintenance  and Support  Services  agreement
  for Fiscal  Year 2025/2026  for the Police  Department  in the amount  of $128,189.53.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Funds  for  these  services  were  included  in  the  Fiscal  Year  2025/26
  Municipal  Budget  in Account  Number  100-513-21-6730.

  ANALYSIS:  This  Purchase  Order  is for  the  renewal  of an existing  sole  source  proprietary
  software  agreement  that does not require  bidding  and complies  with  City  purchasing  guidelines.

  BACKGROUND:  For the past 30 years,  the Police  Department  has contracted  with  Pulsiam  to
  provide  24-hour  support  for  its CAD  and RMS  systems.  The CAD  and RMS  systems  are the
  foundation  of information  technology  that enables  the Police  Department  to receive  9-1-1  calls in
  the dispatch  center  and generate  calls  for service  that are sent electronically  to police  officers  in
  the  field.  The  system  is also  an integrated  database  for  the  processing  and  storage  of  law
  enforcement  information,  including  crime  and arrest reports.

  CAD  and RMS  are an integrated  system  designed  specifically  for law enforcement  operations.
  CAD  is a real-time  system,  which  automatically  verifies  addresses,  tracks,  and manages  incoming
  calls, prioritizes  calls for service,  and tracks  on-duty  personnel  activity.  RMS  provides  reporting
  and analytical  capabilities  for investigations  and generates  statistics  for the Uniform  Crime  Report
  to the State and the Federal  Governments.  Mobile  Data and e-Reporting  modules  allow  officers  to
  access dispatch  information  in the field,  provides  access to our secure law enforcement  network,
  and creates crime  and arrest reports.

  757
 Together,  these modules  create the core of our police  department's  information  system,  which  is
essential  for  the daily  and  efficient  operation  of the police  department.  Maintenance  of this
complex  software  system  is necessary  to keep up with  modifications,  technology  issues, changes
in existing  laws, and other  constantly  evolving  mandates  to law enforcement.
