CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 13, 2026

CALL TO ORDER  Joshua Barron, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:38 p.m.

INVOCATION  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Manuel Arana, Chief of Police

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Joshua Barron, Vice Mayor Al Rios, Council Member Maria del
  Pilar Avalos, Council Member Maria Davila and Council Member Gil
  Hurtado; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Rob Houston, City
  Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

1
BUDGET ADMIN/
ELECTION ADMIN  The City Council considered receiving and filing a presentation on South
  Gate's Budget Status and the Components Required to be Completed to
  Design a Utility Users Tax Measure.

  a. Adopting a Resolution declaring a Fiscal Emergency;

  b. Adopting a Resolution calling a Special Election, request that the Los
  Angeles County Board of Supervisors ("Board of Supervisors")
  authorize the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder / County Clerk
  ("County Elections Official") to render all services necessary to
  conduct the Election, allow for Ballot Arguments, and an Impartial
  Analysis; and

  c. Reviewing the draft Ordinance for voter consideration of the Utility
  Users Tax.

RECESS  Prior to the conclusion of item 1, the City Council recessed at 8:55 p.m.,
  and reconvened at 9:01 p.m., with all Members of Council present.

  Item 1 was unanimously continued to the City Council Meeting of January
  27, 2026, by motion of Council Member Avalos and seconded by Council
  Member Hurtado.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Davila,
  yes; Council Member Hurtado, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 13, 2026

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE-NON-AGENDA
ITEMS – EMAIL  Mario Dominguez criticizes the city’s long-standing failure to properly
  manage the Department of Community Development because it has not
  functioned as an economic engine or supported viable business
  community. He urges the City Council to bring in outside experts to
  overhaul and properly staff the department.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works – nothing to report.

  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation – nothing to
  report.

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development - nothing to report.

  Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services - nothing to report.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Services - nothing to report.

  Manny Arana, Chief of Police - nothing to report.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney - nothing to report.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk - nothing to report.

  Councilmember Avalos reported attending a Vector Control meeting in
  accordance with Assembly Bill 1234, where new officers, including a
  President and Secretary-Treasurer, were appointed and newly elected
  trustees were sworn in. She noted that committee assignments within
  Vector Control will be determined. She reminded residents, due to recent
  rainfall, to remove standing water around their homes to help prevent
  mosquito breeding and related illnesses. She also encouraged the
  community to remain mindful of their health, noting ongoing illness in the
  community, and to take appropriate precautions to protect themselves and
  others.

  Councilmember Davila had no report and extended congratulations to Vice
  Mayor Rios on his retirement.

  Councilmember Hurtado expressed concern regarding recent copper thefts
  affecting Spectrum and Southern California Edison, noting multiple
  service outages in the past week and recent weeks. He suggested exploring
  ways to address the issue, including coordination with the City Attorney,
  Police Department, and District Attorney’s Office, particularly focusing on
  holding purchasers of stolen materials accountable. He also raised public
  safety concerns related to service disruptions impacting residents’ home
  security systems and recommended providing information to the

  Page 2 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 13, 2026

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  community through the City’s social media platforms. He concluded by
  congratulating Vice Mayor Rios on his retirement.

  City Attorney Salinas stated he has been working on this issue with major
  telecommunications company. He has an in-person meeting with Sheriff
  Luna tomorrow afternoon to discuss what they’re doing regarding these
  thefts. There is an Assembly Bill by Mark Gonzalez AB 376 that came
  into effect January 1.

  Vice Mayor Rios commented on recent service outages that prevented
  residents from accessing internet services, noting similar issues in
  neighboring cities. He suggested exploring whether residents may be
  eligible for compensation due to the service interruptions. He also
  expressed concern regarding the continued closure and delayed reopening
  of local libraries and suggested the City consider providing a temporary
  safe space, such as at a park or community facility, where students could
  study and complete homework. Lastly, he inquired about recent activity by
  federal immigration authorities (ICE) in the community and whether the
  Police Department had been contacted regarding their presence.

  Chief Arana stated ICE did contact the Police Department regarding an
  enforcement, but enforcement can mean looking for a criminal as opposed
  to immigration.

  Mayor Barron thanked the department directors for their presentations and
  requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory of Renee Good,
  acknowledging the tragic loss of her life.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 were approved by motion of
  Council Member Davila and seconded by Vice Mayor Rios. Items 2, 5, 8,
  9 and 10 were pulled for separate discussion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes (voted no on 5, 8, 9 & 10);
  Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Hurtado, yes; Vice Mayor
  Rios, yes; Mayor Barron, yes.

2
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  The City Council unanimously adopted Resolution No. 2026-01-CC
  entitled Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  California, initiating the annual proceedings for the levy of the Fiscal Year
  2026/27 assessments and ordering the preparation of an Engineer’s Report
  for the Street Lighting and Landscaping Maintenance District No. 1 during
  consent calendar.

  Page 3 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 13, 2026

3
PERSONNEL BENEFITS/
RETIREMENT ADMIN  The City Council unanimously adopted Resolution No. 2026-02-CC
  entitled A Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  California, during consent calendar certifying that:

  a. Employee is substantially incapacitated from the performance of the
  essential duties of his position;

  b. Employee’s incapacity is a result of industrial (work-related) causes;

  c. Employee is eligible to receive Industrial Disability Retirement
  (“IDR”) benefits through CalPERS; and

  d. The City is not contesting the medical determination of industrial
  disability.

4
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING  The City Council unanimously adopted a list of qualified consultants that
  staff can select from an as-needed basis to provide various services for
  planning, landscaping, environmental, and economic development issues
  during consent calendar.

5
WATER  The City Council approved items A, B, C & D during consent calendar:

  a. Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. 2024-65-CC with Tetra Tech to
  provide additional design services to enhance the design and
  performance of the PFAS Treatment Plant System for the South Gate
  Park Water Wells, City Project No. 666-WTR, in an amount not to
  exceed $142,500;

  b. Appropriate $150,000 in Water Funds to fully fund the design phase
  on the PFAS Treatment Project;

  c. Authorized the City Manager to approve and execute amendments up
  to a cumulative amount of $100,000 from the Water Fund; and

  d. Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 2 to Contract No.
  2024-65-CC in a form acceptable to the City Attorney.

  Page 4 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 13, 2026

6
CITY FACILITIES MGMT  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during consent
  calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2026-02-CC) with Interwest Consulting
  Group, Inc., to provide inspection services for the construction of the
  SGPD HVAC Replacement, City Project No. 667-GEN, in an amount
  not to exceed $84,000; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

7
EMERGENCY/DISASTER
PLANNING/PROGRAMS  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during consent
  calendar:

  a. Professional Services Agreement (Contract No. 2026-03-CC) with
  BOA to prepare design and construction documents for the South Gate
  Emergency Operational Center, City Project No. 582-ARC, for an
  amount not to exceed $129,800; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

8
WATER  The City Council approved items A, B, C & D during consent calendar:

  a. Professional Services Agreement (Contract No. 2026-04-CC) with
  Harper & Associates Engineering, Inc., to prepare design and
  construction documents for the West Side Reservoir Rehabilitation
  Project, City Project No. 742-WTR, in an amount not to exceed
  $48,380;

  b. Amended the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement Program to
  add the West Side Reservoir Rehabilitation Project and appropriate
  $88,380 in Water Funds to fully fund its design phase;

  c. Authorized the City Manager to approve and execute amendments as
  needed to complete the design phase; and

  d. Authorized the Mayor to execute the agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

  Page 5 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 13, 2026

9
WATER  The City Council approved items A, B & C during consent calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2026-05-CC) with Willdan, Inc. to perform
  construction management and inspection services on the Automatic
  Meter Reading Upgrade, Phase V, City Project No. 740-WTR, in an
  amount not-to-exceed $149,574;

  b. Authorized the City Manager to approve and execute amendments to
  the Agreement up to a cumulative amount of $50,000;

  c. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

10
WATER  The City Council approved items A, B, C, D & E during consent calendar

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2026-06-CC) with Gentry General
  Engineering, Inc., to replace 1,659 water meters under the Automatic
  Meter Reading Upgrade, Phase V, City Project No. 740-WTR, in an
  amount not-to-exceed $1,558,203;

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable

  c. Appropriated $2,012,649 from the Water Fund to fully fund the
  Automatic Meter Reading Upgrade, Phase V, City Project No. 740-
  WTR;
  d. Authorized the City Manager to approve and execute amendments to
  the Agreement up to a cumulative amount of $100,000; and

  e. Approved the Notice of Exemption for the Automatic Meter Reading
  Upgrade, Phase V City Project No. 740-WTR.

11

SERVICES  The City Council unanimously authorized the issuance of a Purchase
